# SocialButton

Figma: [02f. SocialButton](https://www.figma.com/design/a7Z956YZy9n6f9uz5DK16Y?node-id=69-894) · Family: 02 Actions · Status: stable · Version 2.0.0 · Updated 2026-05-20

A neutral-container button for third-party sign-in flows. Provides a consistent visual frame for "Continue with Google", "Continue with Apple", "Sign in with Nafath", and similar provider-branded actions. Brand-agnostic by design - drop in any provider logo.

### SocialButton

A neutral, brand-agnostic button for third-party identity and sign-in providers, where the provider logo carries the brand. On Safqah it is mainly the «تسجيل الدخول عبر نفاذ» entry for Nafath identity verification.

Level: organism

Use when:
- Nafath sign-in or KYC identity verification
- Continue with Apple or Google on sign-up and login screens
- Re-authentication from settings: Size=sm with an extended tap area

Don't use when:
- A normal in-app action like Invest or Continue: use Button
- Linking a bank account or IBAN: use Button inside the form flow
- Showing a provider logo without an action: use AbshirLogo, MadaLogo or the relevant logo component

Accessibility: Switch to State=loading immediately on tap to prevent duplicate auth requests, and do not use sm (32dp) as the only sign-in control.

> Not published to the Figma library. Use it by name everywhere; in another Figma file take its published route or copy it from the Syntropy file (syntropy-components, unpublished.md).

## Guide from the doc page

### Overview

SocialButton is the visual container for third-party sign-in actions. It provides a consistent neutral frame (white background, subtle border, brand-agnostic text) so that any provider logo - Google, Apple, Facebook, Nafath, Absher - can drop in without competing with the Safqah brand or with each other.

On Safqah, SocialButton is used most often on sign-up flows, login screens, and KYC verification (especially Nafath for Saudi identity). The neutral container keeps the visual focus on the provider logo while maintaining typographic consistency with the rest of the app.

### At a glance

| Large · sign-up flow | Medium · login screen | Small · inline action |
| --- | --- | --- |

### Anatomy

SocialButton has a simple slot structure - one icon, one label, neutral container. The container chrome stays consistent across providers so users build muscle memory for "sign-in zone".

| Icon (leading) Provider logo (Google G, Apple, Facebook f, Nafath wordmark). 20dp at lg/md, 16dp at sm. Instance-swap with any Syntropy or provider-supplied icon. | Label Action text. Default "Continue with Provider" - override per instance ("Continue with Google", "تسجيل دخول عبر نفاذ"). Bound to text/default token. | Container bg/surface fill, border/default 1dp stroke, Radius/8 corners. Neutral by design - provider brand color belongs ON the icon, not the container. | Padding & gap Spacing/24 (lg) / Spacing/16 (md) / Spacing/12 (sm) horizontal padding. Spacing/12 gap between icon and label across all sizes. |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |

### Sizes

Three sizes match Button conventions. Pick based on context - large for primary sign-up flows, medium for standard login screens, small for inline actions or tight layouts.

lg

Height 48 · padding 24 · icon 20 · font 16

Primary sign-up / first-time login. Most visual weight - use when the sign-in is the main action on screen.

md

Height 40 · padding 16 · icon 20 · font 14

Standard login screen with multiple providers. Balances visibility with vertical space - most common choice.

sm

Height 32 · padding 12 · icon 16 · font 14

Inline secondary actions, settings-screen re-auth, or tight layouts. Lowest emphasis.

### States

Six states cover the full lifecycle. Each uses a different combination of background, border, and text/icon color to communicate the current interaction state.

default

bg/surface

Resting state. White container with subtle border. Ready to receive input.

hover

bg/brand/lightest-hover

Cursor over (desktop). Subtle brand-green tint plus stronger border edge.

pressed

bg/brand/lightest-pressed

Tap acknowledged. Slightly darker tint than hover. Brief flash.

focused

bg/surface + 2dp focus ring

Keyboard focus. 2dp outset stroke using border/focus. Visible against any background.

disabled

bg/disabled

Inert. Gray fill with muted icon and text. Cannot be activated.

loading

bg/surface (icon muted)

Auth in progress. Icon opacity 0.4 + label color text/muted. Replace icon with spinner at instance time.

### Direction - LTR and RTL

SocialButton inherits the Direction axis from the broader Safqah system. In LTR contexts (English), the icon sits leading (left) and the label trails (right). In RTL contexts (Arabic), the order flips - icon trails (right), label leads (left).

LTR

Default. Icon leading, label trailing. Natural reading order for English/Latin scripts.

RTL

Arabic context. Label leading, icon trailing. Critical for Nafath, Absher, and any Arabic-language sign-in flow.

### Code examples

How to consume SocialButton in production code.

### Flutter

```dart
// Continue with Google (medium, default state)
SafqahSocialButton(
  provider: SocialProvider.google,
  label: 'Continue with Google',
  size: SafqahSocialButtonSize.md,
  onPressed: () => _signInWithGoogle(),
)

// Sign in with Apple (large, required iOS treatment)
SafqahSocialButton(
  provider: SocialProvider.apple,
  label: 'Sign in with Apple',
  size: SafqahSocialButtonSize.lg,
  onPressed: () => _signInWithApple(),
)

// Nafath (Saudi national identity) - RTL Arabic context
Directionality(
  textDirection: TextDirection.rtl,
  child: SafqahSocialButton(
    provider: SocialProvider.nafath,
    label: 'تسجيل دخول عبر نفاذ',
    size: SafqahSocialButtonSize.lg,
    onPressed: () => _verifyWithNafath(),
  ),
)

// Loading state - tap registered, auth in flight
SafqahSocialButton(
  provider: SocialProvider.google,
  label: 'Continue with Google',
  state: SafqahSocialButtonState.loading,
  onPressed: null,
)
```

### React (token-driven)

```dart
<SafqahSocialButton
  provider="google"
  label="Continue with Google"
  size="md"
  onClick={signInWithGoogle}
/>

<SafqahSocialButton
  provider="apple"
  label="Sign in with Apple"
  size="lg"
  onClick={signInWithApple}
/>

<SafqahSocialButton
  provider="nafath"
  label="تسجيل دخول عبر نفاذ"
  size="lg"
  dir="rtl"
  onClick={verifyWithNafath}
/>
```

### Usage - Do and Don't

Concrete Safqah scenarios paired with their wrong counterparts.

- **Do** · Sign-up screen - primary provider: Large size (48 dp) for the primary sign-up flow. The lg height matches a primary Button - visually equivalent emphasis, so users understand this is a key action.
- **Don't** · Sign-up screen - primary provider: Don't use sm size as the only sign-in path. 32 dp fails WCAG 2.5.5 touch target and reads as a secondary action, not a primary one.
- **Do** · Tap registered - auth in flight: Switch to loading state immediately on tap. Icon mutes to opacity 0.4, label stays in place. At instance time, swap the icon for a Spinner Syntropy icon for animation.
- **Don't** · Tap registered - auth in flight: Don't leave the button in default state after tap. Users will tap again, thinking it didn't register - causing duplicate auth requests.
- **Do** · Nafath verification - Arabic context: Direction=rtl flips the visual order - label leads, icon trails. DOM order stays consistent for screen readers. Required for Arabic Saudi flows.
- **Don't** · Nafath verification - Arabic context: Don't use LTR variant in Arabic context. Icon ends up on the left, label on the right - breaks reading order and looks foreign in an Arabic-first app.
- **Do** · Inactive auth method: Disabled state grays the container and mutes the icon + text. Use when a provider is temporarily unavailable (outage) or when the user has already linked that provider.
- **Don't** · Inactive auth method: Don't leave an unavailable provider in the default state. Users will tap it and hit an error - frustrating UX. Either disable visually or remove it entirely.

### Notes from the maintainer

Implementation decisions, trade-offs, and things to watch out for.

> **Info:** Icon defaults to Button Icon Placeholder. At consumption time, swap to a real provider logo via the Icon instance-swap property. Logos should be in their official brand colors (Google G in multi-color, Apple in black, Facebook f in blue) - the container is neutral specifically so the icon can carry the provider brand.

> **Tip:** No "provider" axis baked into the component. This is deliberate - adding a Provider variant axis would lock the component to a fixed list of providers and require a release to add new ones (Nafath today, who knows tomorrow). Instance-swap on the icon keeps it open-ended.

> **Warning:** Loading state is static in Figma - no spinner animation. At instance time, swap the icon to a Spinner Syntropy icon (when available) for the actual loading visual. The opacity 0.4 + muted label communicate "in progress" until the animated swap happens.

> **Warning:** Apple HIG technically requires a black-filled "Sign in with Apple" button (and dark mode variants). We don't enforce that - Safqah uses a single neutral container for all providers for visual consistency. If Apple compliance review pushes back, build a separate ApplePrimary variant or override the bg via instance.

> **Info:** Hover and pressed states use bg/brand/lightest-hover and bg/brand/lightest-pressed. These tokens are mildly brand-tinted (light green) - consistent with how other neutral Safqah components react to interaction. If a fully-neutral hover (gray) is needed later, add bg/hover/subtle and bg/pressed/subtle tokens to the Semantic collection.

> **Warning:** sm size (32 dp) fails WCAG 2.5.5 touch target. Flag every sm usage for review. Acceptable inline (e.g. "Reconnect" inside a settings list with extended tap region), never as the primary sign-in CTA.
